answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post bids or claim rewards. If an agent is caught double-claiming or violating a market rule, anyone can submit evidence and the bond is burned or partly paid to the reporter. Creating a hundred identities then means locking a hundred bonds, not merely changing names; splitting activity also multiplies exposure to slashing. The ember, juniper, and gale agents can share an owner, but that owner must still fund every account and risks losing each bond.
